ambiguities.aspect: comparison condition on equality (greater vs greater-or-equal)
readings: Quotient bit = 1 only when the extracted dividend bits are strictly greater than B; when they are equal the quotient bit is 0 and no subtraction is performed (remainder = extracted bits)
Quotient bit = 1 when the extracted bits are >= B (normal restoring division); when they are equal the quotient bit is 1 and the remainder becomes 0
Since both always blocks are declared combinational and triggered by A and B, result and odd are pure combinational functions of A and B valid in the same cycle as the inputs
Because the first block is described as loading A and B into registers a_reg/b_reg, result and odd are registered and are only valid one clock cycle after A/B change (the module is clocked)

ambiguities.aspect: width of the running remainder versus the 8-bit divisor
readings: The remainder is kept 9 bits wide (8-bit remainder concatenated with the next dividend bit) and B is zero-extended to 9 bits for the compare/subtract, so a remainder with MSB=1 is handled correctly
The concatenated value is truncated back to 8 bits to 'match the bit width of the divisor', discarding the MSB, which changes every subsequent compare/subtract and the final odd

ambiguities.aspect: remainder value when the extracted bits are not greater than B
readings: The running remainder is left unchanged (the extracted dividend bits are kept as the remainder for the next iteration)
The remainder is forced to 0, taking 'use the difference as the remainder' literally with a difference of 0 when no subtraction occurs
